en.bestFor: Explaining one concept with a single character: a surprised close-up first, then a seated interview facing the camera.
en.structure: Clip 1 is a 3–4 second close-up. Each later clip is 3–8 seconds and covers one point. Clip count follows the duration preset.
en.hook: Opens with the camera above, then drops down and snaps a zoom-in on the surprised face. The person stays upright. Sharp and clear. One short hook line.
en.arc: After the close-up, cut once to the same person seated in a medium interview shot. From clip 3 on, each clip starts on the previous clip's end. The last line rests in the chair.
en.narrator: Exactly one character speaks every line to the camera. A pasted script is read in order. A concept with no script becomes interview lines for you to approve.
en.visual: Look and palette come from the chosen visual style. Clip 1 stays upright: the camera starts above and drops down while zooming in. From clip 2 the same person sits right-side up, facing the lens, in the same chair, background, and light. On-canvas type is a shock poster: bold condensed white letters, yellow numbers, and a yellow dry-brush stroke behind the payoff.
en.audio: No background music. Only the character's voice. The spoken line is the on-canvas shock type.
en.rules: Needs exactly one character and an aspect ratio. No second person, no screen recording, and no new location after the seat is set. Clip 1 is the only framing change.
